oracle: tests/e2e/flask_oracle.py through a one-line factory wrapper (redash.app.create_app()), 2026-11-19, Flask 3.1.3 under the pin's own environment, with `redis.from_url` replaced by a stub whose info() reports 7.0.0 and whose get/hget return None (no Redis service here; REDASH_DATABASE_URL=sqlite://, dummy secrets) -- the url_map itself is redash's own. It lists 100 rules (153 method pairs): 71 rules (118 pairs) are Flask-RESTful resources (`api.add_org_resource`, 67 calls in redash/handlers/api.py) which this catalog does NOT read; 1 is Flask's own /static; 28 rules (34 pairs) are core Flask registrations. Sextant reads 7 of those 28 (google_oauth 3, ldap_auth 1, remote_user_auth 1, saml_auth 2): blueprints built in the same module as their routes. It misses the other 21: every `@routes.route(...)` in redash/handlers/*.py, because `routes = Blueprint(...)` is built in redash/handlers/base.py and imported (a blueprint imported from another module has no owner, so the flask catalog does not match; measured on a two-file project). Of Sextant's 11 inbound rows, 3 are the oidc blueprint (create_oidc_blueprint returns nothing unless OIDC is configured, so the oracle run has none) and 5 carry `(unresolved)` for the path, because org_scoped_rule() branches on settings.MULTI_ORG (a deployment value, so not evaluated). Every row was matched to a Blueprint.route registration in redash/authentication/{google_oauth,oidc,saml_auth,remote_user_auth,ldap_auth}.py. The 50 outbound rows are Sextant's own output, spot-checked against source (version.redash.io, tinybird, yandex_disk, datadog, google userinfo), not reviewed line by line.
